newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares falter on profit-taking, shed 0.29pct.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares falter on profit-taking, shed 0.29pct.

text.p: A flurry of profit-taking pulled the Athens bourse's benchmark index down 0.29 percent on Friday with industrials bucking a drift in banks.
The Athens general index finished 4.72 points lower at 1,638.79 from Thursday's 1,643.51 close, having fluctuated between 1,640 and 1,650 in active trading.
Upbeat Hellenic Bottling led industrials 0.54 percent higher, helping to cushion a 0.78 percent drop in banks.
The constrasting performance in banks and industrials was seen by brokers as the result of a slight shift in buying interest.
"Banks continue to dominate the scene but a shift in investor interest towards large and middle cap industrials has been noted," said Nick Stathopoulos, broker at N.Devletoglou Securities.
Friday's slide did not unnerve market participants who are adamant on its upside potential.
"It is natural for the market to take a breather after a rally which has stretched for quite a while," said Stathopoulos.

"The market is very strong overall with insatiable buying interest and appears overbought only because it has not had the time to digest the prolonged rally," said a broker at another major securities house."
Mild price corrections are easily turned around as investors flock in and the market keeps on hearing improved macroeconomic numbers, the broker added.
Customer business at the 1330 local count amounted to 29.7 billion drachmas in volume of 6.7 million shares.

Block trading was very active, including Hellenic Bottling, total 137,740 shares at 10,700 drachmas, Alpha Credit Bank, 35,000 shares at 21,400, Ionian Bank, 12,500 shares at 8,300, Viohalko, 16,000 shares at 6,500, National Bank, 3,000 shares at 34,200-34,250, Intracom common, 21,000 shares at 12,400, Intracom preferred, 17,000 shares at 9,500, and Greek Progress Fund, 50,000 shares at 2,915.
Decliners beat advancers 117 to 104 with 34 stocks unchanged on 255 traded.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted lower at 1,092-1,122. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, firmed 60 drachmas to 6,605.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $86.85-$88.55. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted lower at 3,591-3,814 drachmas.
The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $21.47-N/O. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4 (c) Reuters Limited 1997
